passages.note: Bill overview page shows Carter as a co-sponsor of HB2492 and that the Governor signed it as Chapter 99.
House Third Reading roll call on HB2492 lists Carter voting Y; the division (26 No) is far from near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship as prescribed in section 16-166, subsection F, and the county recorder or other officer in charge of elections shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship
passages.note: Chaptered text of HB2492, a single-subject registration-verification act whose operative sections condition registration on evidence of citizenship.

rows.reasoning: Carter co-sponsored HB2492 (2022) and voted Y on its House Third Reading, a single-subject registration bill whose operative text provides that "any application for registration shall be accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship" and that the recorder "shall reject any application for registration that is not accompanied by satisfactory evidence of citizenship", and that a resident may register only if the resident "Is a citizen of the United States and has provided SATISFACTORY evidence of CITIZENSHIP as PRESCRIBED in section 16-166". That is the rung "Require documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote." The 2022 act falls within his earlier House term in this same legislature, so it is in-term under the V5 ruling.
